strengths_deep_dive: Rebuilding Alliance excels in direct service delivery despite its small cash footprint. The organization has provided critical support to <cite id="2">hundreds of children</cite> through the Al Aqaba kindergarten and maintains an <cite id="3">ongoing presence in military courts</cite> to monitor the representation of children. Their <cite id="4">advocacy for building permits</cite> and demolition prevention provides a unique legal safeguard for families in the West Bank. These efforts are supported by a <cite id="14">90.3% independent board of directors</cite>, ensuring high levels of internal oversight and governance.
rich_narrative.summary: Rebuilding Alliance is a humanitarian and advocacy organization dedicated to protecting Palestinian rights and providing direct relief in the Gaza Strip, West Bank, and Jerusalem. The organization reported <cite id="15">$825,817 in total revenue in FY2023</cite>, though more recent filings show a significant increase to <cite id="14">$4,309,990 in FY2024</cite>. While the charity maintains a high <cite id="14">program expense ratio of 90.3%</cite>, its financial stability is a primary concern. In FY2024, the organization operated with <cite id="14">negative working capital of -2.7 months</cite>, indicating that its current liabilities exceed its liquid assets. Furthermore, a substantial portion of its revenue is driven by noncash contributions. In FY2024, <cite id="14">84% of revenue consisted of noncash items</cite>, which can inflate efficiency metrics while leaving the organization with limited cash for operations. Despite these financial pressures, the charity continues to deliver essential services, including <cite id="5">hot meals programs</cite> and the distribution of <cite id="1">27,000 solar lanterns</cite> to families in need. Its work also includes <cite id="4">advocacy to prevent home demolitions</cite> and supporting <cite id="1">140 children in schools</cite> facing legal challenges.
